name: Introduction and overview — V-22 Osprey — aircraft record
title: Introduction and overview — V-22 Osprey
description: Introduction and overview of the V-22 Osprey: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history. The V-22 Osprey is a twin-engine tiltrotor aircraft built by Bell and Boeing, entering service in 2007. Its engine nacelles rotate to transition between helicopter vertical flight and faster fixed-wing cruise — twice the speed and five times the range of the helicopters it replaced. Over 400 have been built for the Marines, Air Force, and Navy. Baseline facts: Tiltrotor aircraft; service from 2007; 400+ built by Bell/Boeing; vertical takeoff, airplane cruise..
how_it_works: Wings generate lift from airflow; the engine provides thrust; control surfaces and fly-by-wire or mechanical controls steer the aircraft in three axes.
key_points: V-22 Osprey: What this aircraft is, its role, and why it matters in aviation history.
Tiltrotor aircraft; service from 2007; 400+ built by Bell/Boeing; vertical takeoff, airplane cruise.
Key figure: 316 mph cruise, twice helicopter speed; two Rolls-Royce T406 turboshafts; rotating nacelles.
